Peerless is a long-established California commercial almond variety producing large, plump, soft-shell kernels with good flavor, historically planted widely for its productivity and reliable performance in California's Central Valley almond-growing regions. The tree blooms relatively late compared to some other varieties, offering some protection against early spring frost damage to the crop, a real practical advantage in marginal or frost-prone sites. Water deeply and regularly through the growing season, particularly during kernel fill in summer, and harvest once hulls split open in late summer to early fall, allowing nuts to dry before storage.

Sonora is a California almond variety valued for large, attractive, very soft-shell kernels that crack open easily by hand, along with sweet, well-flavored nutmeat that makes it popular for home orchards and specialty markets alike. The tree blooms early, which gives it a head start on the growing season but also increases exposure to spring frost risk during flowering, so site selection matters for reliable annual crops. Water deeply and regularly through the growing season, especially during kernel development, and harvest once hulls split open in late summer, allowing the nuts to dry thoroughly before storage to prevent mold.

Ne Plus Ultra is one of the oldest named California almond varieties still in cultivation, its name Latin for 'nothing further beyond,' reflecting the confidence of its 19th-century breeders in its quality, and it remains valued for a long, slender, soft-shell kernel with good sweet flavor. Historically an important variety in the early development of California's commercial almond industry, it has since been surpassed in commercial volume by more productive modern releases but is still grown by home orchardists and specialty producers who appreciate its distinctive nut shape and historic pedigree. Water deeply through the growing season, especially during kernel fill, and harvest once hulls split open in late summer.

The medium, hard-shell nut has good flavor and the tree is a consistent, productive bearer, valued in commercial orchards as much for its reliable pollination role as for its own direct nut production.
